Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple of clarifying points from our side: 

1) On PII: we cannot allow any PII to be persisted outside our environment. Model prompts may contain PHI/PII; we need to ensure the inference runtime can be configured to avoid writing user text to persistent storage. Are there knobs to disable token logging or to store logs only in masked/hashed form?

2) Egress: AcmeHealth requires no outbound connections from the inference subnet to the public internet. We can allow connections to our internal telemetry endpoint (https://telemetry.acmehealth.internal) and to our internal KMS. Can Redwood operate in a fully private VPC with those constraints, or would you require a NAT for any agent?

3) Air-gapped/on-prem: For high-risk environments we may require an on-prem appliance. Is there a migration path from Private (VPC) to on-prem air-gapped later?

Also looping in our security team (security@acmehealth.com) for audit questions.

Hi Tom / Jill —

Thanks for the clarity. Short answers up front, details below:

1) PII persistence: Supported. In Private VPC mode we can configure the inference runtime to avoid writing user text to disk. Token-level logging can be disabled; application logs can be emitted as structured, masked events only (PII fields hashed). We also support a policy to send only aggregated telemetry (no prompts) to any external telemetry endpoint.

2) Egress / Network boundaries: We support fully private VPC deployments. Outbound traffic can be restricted to a small set of customer-controlled endpoints (your internal telemetry endpoint and KMS). No NAT to public internet is required. We use a control-plane connector for management; this connector can be run either through an outbound-only management tunnel (customer-approved IPs) or via a private peering arrangement. For strict air-gapped setups, control plane can be handled via an on-prem agent and all updates delivered by an offline package.

3) On-prem / air-gapped path: Yes. We have an on-prem appliance offering (private build) with HSM/KMS integrations and manual update cadence. Migration path: start in Private VPC to validate behavior (2-4 weeks), then target on-prem delivery (timeline ~6-10 weeks depending on approvals & network staging).

Extra notes on logs/retention:
- Retention controls: log retention configurable per-customer; we can set 12 months by policy.
- Masking: we support both client-side hashing (recommended) and server-side structured masking where we never store raw prompt text.
- KV cache: in-memory by default; optional on-disk cache can be disabled in your deployment.

I attached an updated diagram (rwi_private_vpc_arch_diagram.png) and our SOC2 summary for your security team. Happy to hop on a technical call with your infra/security folks tomorrow.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
